brief: Standard Chartered's October 2026 Global Market Outlook argues that strong AI-investment-driven growth lets the global economy absorb an oil-price shock and a synchronized central bank hiking cycle, so equities can keep focusing on earnings strength. The Fed, ECB and BoJ all hiked in September 2026, the first time on record all three moved in the same month, responding to energy-driven inflation. SC expects the Fed to hike twice more (fed funds to 4.5% by June 2027), the ECB once more (to 2.75%), and the BoJ once a quarter to 2% by mid-2027, before cuts begin in H2 2027 as oil and tariff effects fade. SC argues 1990s hiking-into-growth is the right parallel, not 2022's inflation surprise, so earnings growth should outweigh the valuation drag from higher yields, and any pullback into US mid-term elections is a buying opportunity. It stays Overweight equities over bonds and cash (Overweight US and Asia ex-Japan, Taiwan the only regional equity Overweight, China trimmed to Core), prefers credit over duration, holds gold Overweight, and flags oil above USD 120-150/bbl as the key risk to the growth call.
